subject.title: Enhancement: Allow custom safe headers in fetch-guard cross-origin redirects

question: Should OpenClaw add an operator-controlled way to retain custom headers such as x-api-key across cross-origin fetch-guard redirects, and must it be scoped by destination origin rather than a global safe-header extension?
rationale: The request intentionally changes a credential-forwarding boundary and adds public config surface, so automation cannot choose the acceptable trust model or guardrails.

options.title: Design scoped operator policy
options.body: Allow the capability only with maintainer-approved header validation, HTTPS and destination-origin scoping, docs, and tests that preserve strict defaults.

options.title: Keep strict stripping only
options.body: Reject the new config surface and continue dropping non-standard headers on all cross-origin redirects.

options.title: Add global header extension list
options.body: Implement the requested additionalSafeHeaders shape directly, accepting the higher risk that allowed headers can replay to any redirect origin.

recommendation.title: Design scoped operator policy
recommendation.body: Allow the capability only with maintainer-approved header validation, HTTPS and destination-origin scoping, docs, and tests that preserve strict defaults.

likelyOwner.reason: The strict behavior traces to steipete's security hardening commit, and the remaining choice changes that trust boundary.
